blocks.html: Short answer: Chanthaburi blends a riverside old town, beaches and fruit orchards. For culture stay in the Chanthaboon riverside community (heritage houses, the gem market and great food); for the sea head to Chao Lao / Laem Sadet beach with its seafront resorts; for nature and durian orchards go up toward Khao Khitchakut and the waterfalls (busiest in fruit season, April–June).

faq.q: Where should I stay in Chanthaburi?
faq.a: For the old town and good food, the Chanthaboon riverside community is best — wander the heritage houses, the gem market and the cathedral. For the beach, head to Chao Lao–Laem Sadet; in fruit season (April–June), durian-orchard trips lean toward Khao Khitchakut.

faq.q: Where to stay for the Chanthaburi gem market?
faq.a: The gem market is in the old-town area next to the Chanthaboon riverside community, so staying nearby lets you walk there. It is liveliest Friday to Sunday when traders deal stones along the street — an unusual sight and fun to photograph.

faq.q: How many days in Chanthaburi, and can I combine it with Trat?
faq.a: Two days suits the old town plus a beach day. Many drive on to Trat or Koh Chang to the east, about 1.5 hours away, making an easy eastern-seaboard trip.
